note: Hash lines are exact. "from" is the version the old hash belonged to, the block version is where the new hash starts (blocks without "to" in the source are filed under 3.2, the newest version the Vonksdesu data covers, and their "from" is the label upstream gave). Chains exist (a -> b -> c) and loops exist (a hash can come back), so resolve with a visited set. "current": true means the new hash is in the hefeng 3.3 hash table. Conflicts are listed at the end with what was chosen.

rules.detail: Jane Doe 2.5: the Hair component was split into Hair (hair meshes) and Arms (hands and accessories) and the bone order changed. Remap the 4 u32 bone indices of the blend buffer (vb2 stride 32, weights untouched) with map_hair for the Hair blend hash and map_arms for the Arms blend hash. Blend hashes: Hair e42171df, Arms d06a9206; the old position hashes 33a09cfe and 82e7c056 map to them (position_to_blend). The Vonksdesu remapper finds the buffer from the section with that hash (position hash is accepted and converted) via its vb2 resource (stride 32); if no known hash is present it falls back to every stride 32 vb2 buffer whose resource name contains hair/head (map_hair) or hand/finger/accessor/knife (map_arms). Not automatable from this data alone: the ini also needs the Hair sections duplicated as Arms sections (hashes in the Jane hash.json of the assets repo), the Position section turned into a Blend section, and the HairA DrawIndexed calls split by hand (see the Satan1c wiki page Jane 2.5 fix). Only the buffer remap is exact.

Dialyn body: remap the 4 u32 bone indices of the blend buffer bound to blend hash 3d7e53cf (position hash ff36809b converts to it), stride 32, weights untouched. The same table is in the hefeng tool VGX list (old and new lists), so two sources agree.

rules.character: 46 characters, 53 face and eyebrow meshes (list in texcoord_hashes)
rules.detail: Face texcoord buffer (vb1) layout change in 3.2. COLOR was 4 x uint8 (R8G8B8A8_UNORM), now 4 x float32. Per vertex: old 36 bytes = 4B color + 2f + 2f + 2f + 2f, new 48 bytes = 4f color + same 32 bytes. Convert: color[i] = byte[i] / 255.0 as f32 little endian, then copy the remaining 32 bytes unchanged. Then in the [Resource] section bound to vb1 change "stride = 36" to "stride = 48" (keep the old line commented). Gate: only run when a TextureOverride in the ini has hash = one of texcoord_hashes (the 3.2 texcoord hash, so run the hash replacement first). Find the buffer through the vb1 line of that section or of a command list it runs (recursively), then Resource filename. Idempotent: bytes per vertex = file size / vertex count (from the blend buffer, size / 32); 36 means convert, 48 means already fixed, anything else means skip and report. Back up the .buf first.
rules.tool: https://github.com/hefengchang/ZZZ-Model-Fix-Tool (ZZZ Index and Vertex Fix Tool, mode 2) and the same list in https://github.com/Vonksdesu/ZZZ-Mod-Fixer/tree/gui-version

rules.character: any (needs a reference), bundled: Dialyn body, Ellen legs
rules.detail: Bone index remap in a blend buffer (vb2, stride 32 per vertex = 4 x f32 weights + 4 x u32 bone indices). Rewrite only the 4 u32 indices through an old -> new table, leave the weights as they are. The tables for Dialyn and Ellen are in the Dialyn and Ellen vertex group rules. For other meshes the hefeng tool derives the table by matching mod vertices to a game dump (needs gui_collect dumps): spatial grid with cell size 0.01 game units, up to 6 nearest mod vertices per game vertex, each pair votes mod index -> game index when both weights in the same sorted slot are >= 0.01 and differ by <= 0.05, votes resolved greedily and one to one, skip the mesh if fewer than 5 percent of game vertices matched, flag entries with fewer than 20 votes. This needs the game dump, so it cannot be done from the JSON alone.

Texture twins. ZZZ uses a different texture hash for the same texture at 1024p and 2048p (and a few legacy variants). For each entry: if the ini has a TextureOverride with hash = <hash> and none of the hashes in copy_for exists anywhere in the ini, copy that whole section (keep its lines, drop its hash line) into a new TextureOverride with hash = copy_for[0] (name it after the first plus ".Copy" or similar). Then also treat the new hash as seen. Ini text edit only, harmless when the section already exists.

IB stubs. If the ini has a TextureOverride for one of the texture hashes in if_any_of and no section for the IB hash "ib" (nor its older hash, resolved through the hash list), append "[TextureOverride<Name>IB]", "hash = <ib>", "match_priority = 0". The upstream code gives no reason. Low risk and low value, so apply it only when the mod has no IB section for that part at all. Ini text edit only.

Legacy slot overrides to SlotFix names, so the textures stay right when slots move and no hash is needed. In every active ini, ps-t3 = X becomes "Resource\ZZMI\Diffuse = ref X", ps-t4 NormalMap, ps-t5 LightMap, ps-t6 MaterialMap. After the last of a run of those lines add "run = CommandList\ZZMI\SetTextures" at the same indent. ps-t17 = X becomes "Resource\RabbitFX\GlowMap = ref X" and ps-t18 "Resource\RabbitFX\FXMap = ref X". Skip files whose name contains disabled, slotfix or rabbitfx and folders with those names. Needs ZZMI Package (SlotFix, Resources.ini) or RabbitFX 6 installed, which XXMI ships. Ini text edit only. The Vonksdesu fixer instead adds "run = CommandListSkinTexture" after match_first_index lines (788 triggers). That list is a legacy ZZMI name that current packages do not define, so do not port it; use the SlotFix form above.

rules.detail: Model changes that an ini edit cannot repair. The hefeng log marks these as "model changed, not fixable": Wise swimwear hair (IB cb272754 -> 0ec31440) and body (4fe696c8 -> 19a3f02e), Belle neck IB 62ed56cc -> d0627e1f, Jane hair weights changed (also see the Jane rule), Roxy hair/face split (3.21: object_indexes [0, 12435, 14712] -> [0, 11700] hair, [0, 7350, 9216] -> [0, 6996, 9216] face). Show these as "needs an update from the mod author", do not edit.

upstream.notes: Sections "N.N -> N.N" (the word 版本 may precede), blocks start with "【names】" (English names concatenated after the Chinese, "/" separated), then lines "IB: <ib> [-> <new ib>]（part）" followed by indented "field: old -> new" lines (draw_vb, position_vb, texcoord_vb, blend_vb, Diffuse, NormalMap, LightMap, MaterialMap, with optional 1024 or 2048 suffix; older sections use Position, Texcoord, Blend, VertexLimit). Lines starting with a star are notes. Newest section is on top. Best single place for new ZZZ versions: it was updated for 3.3 on 2026-11-10.

upstream.format: json directory listing, then one json per character
upstream.notes: Current hashes per character: array of components with component_name, draw_vb, position_vb, texcoord_vb, blend_vb, ib, object_indexes and texture_hashes [[ [type, ext, hash] ]]. A hash found in a mod ini that is absent from every file but present as "old" in the log is a confirmed broken hash. Use the git commit history of a file to get old values when the log is late.

{"version":"3.2","characters":{Name:{"components":{"Alice Hair IB Hash":{"current_hash":"..","history":[{"version":"1.1","hash":"old","migrated_to":"current"}]}}}}}. Old hash to current hash with chains already collapsed, regenerated automatically (last commit 2026-11-13). hash_migrations.json (3 MB, same folder) has the action list per hash. No licence stated, so use it as a pointer and a cross-check, not as shipped data.

Each file returns {hash: [(command, args), ...]}. Parse with the python ast module or a regex, never import or run it. Commands: log, update_hash(new), multiply_section_if_missing, add_section_if_missing, add_ib_check_if_missing, zzz_13_remap_texcoord, zzz_12_shrink_texcoord_color, update_buffer_blend_indices, transfer_indexed_sections. The gui-version branch is the live one; main is frozen at 3.0.

Satan1c fork is the freshest (pushed 2026-11-11, the leotorrez repo stopped on 2026-09-20). Automatic fixes from this: walk the commits that touch PlayerCharacterData/<Char>/hash.json, diff component by component (draw_vb, position_vb, texcoord_vb, blend_vb, ib, object_indexes, texture_hashes), each changed value is an old -> new pair. This is what VersionFixerGenerator in ZZMI_tools does.
